newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 20.

text.p: Plan for welfare informants to tell all: Social Welfare Minister Roger Sowry was asked on Thursday night to appoint a "highly respected" person to investigate claims that welfare staff falsified documents about the deaths of children in their care. Page 1.

High Court asked to rule on election spending row: The Electoral Commission has asked the High Court for a ruling on campaign spending after ACT NZ refused to give an itemised account of where its money went last election. Page 2.

'Good shape economy' will show in Budget, says Peters: Treasurer Winston Peters promised on Thursday that his and the Coalition Government's first Budget would prove that the economy was "in good shape". Page 2.
Saturn takes on Telecom in local calls: Petone-based cable television company Saturn will become the first company to offer a local residential phone service in competition with Telecom. Page 13.
MPs complain about being called 'sleazy': "Please don't call us sleazy," was the indignant howl from New Zealand First and National MPs in Parliament on Thursday. Page 3.

Minister under fire for 'gaffes': Associate Health Minister Neil Kirton was under fire on two fronts on Thursday, from the Tobacco Institute and the Labour Party accusing him of mounting unwarranted attacks. Page 8.
NZIT tries investing in Australia: New Zealand Investment Trust has begun investing in Australian shares. Page 16.
Newmarket Property Trust downgrades profit forecast 60pc: Newmarket Property Trust on Thursday sharply downgraded its annual profit to June 30. Page 16.

Mill decision disappoints farmers: United Wheatgrowers and Federated Farmers' arable section say they are disappointed that Goodman Fielder had approval to buy the New Zealand assets of Defiance Mills. Page 16.

Youths in cells 'unacceptable': A hard-hitting reports to the Minister of Social Welfare suggests the head of his department, Margaret Bazley, may be failing in her legal duty to provide enough beds for young offenders.
Surplus warning: The Treasurer, Winston Peters, on Thursday warned economic analysts to "moderate" their Budget surplus projections for the coming financial year.
Sky signals $800m float for end of year: Sky TV's owners have been courting sharebrokers with a view to an $800 million float.
Philips charges dismissed: Former Pacer Kerridge executive chairman David Phillips had three charges against him of fraud and one of perjury dismissed on Thursday.
